research_mode: official ONS and Office for Statistics Regulation sources only; recording-quality governance, inspection, rule-change, survey-design and uncertainty gates; no parcel result or safety score claimed

sources.name: Training and guidance control
verified_claims: regular training and clear guidance support more accurate and consistent recording
training has addressed burglary, theft-from-person and domestic-abuse recording issues
limitations: training effectiveness varies by implementation and force

sources.name: Centralised recording model
verified_claims: many consulted forces view a dedicated central crime-management unit as best practice
limitations: the review sample covered nine forces and may not generalise to all forces

sources.name: Centralised quality control
verified_claims: centralised crime-management units give forces greater control over data quality than relying only on frontline entry
limitations: centralisation does not validate every record automatically

sources.name: Centralised rule interpretation
verified_claims: a smaller dedicated recording team is more likely to apply counting rules consistently than thousands of frontline officers
limitations: the claim is a process rationale rather than a national effect estimate

sources.name: Centralisation insufficiency
verified_claims: centralisation is not the only recording model and does not by itself guarantee accurate and consistent recording
limitations: candidate scoring must not treat centralisation as a force-quality proxy

sources.name: Validation resource constraint
verified_claims: crime volume and resource constraints can prevent forces from validating every crime record
limitations: absence of full validation does not identify which individual records are wrong

sources.name: Point-of-call validation
verified_claims: recording and validating crime close to the initial call can improve control but requires significant resource

sources.name: Multi-force complexity
verified_claims: 44 police forces may manage crime recording in different ways
limitations: national aggregation can conceal force-level process variation

sources.name: Interacting quality factors
verified_claims: recording decisions, guidance changes, IT systems and quality assurance all influence police-recorded-crime quality
limitations: the factors can interact differently across forces and over time

sources.name: Metropolitan Police national influence
verified_claims: Metropolitan Police recorded about one-sixth of all crimes excluding fraud and computer misuse in the year ending December 2023
limitations: quality issues in a large force can disproportionately affect national totals

sources.name: Administrative-data residual error
verified_claims: operational administrative data cannot have all inaccuracies and inconsistencies eliminated
limitations: quality controls reduce but do not remove residual error

sources.name: Domestic-abuse flag consistency
verified_claims: domestic-abuse flags are manually applied and can be interpreted inconsistently within and across forces
limitations: flag inconsistency affects contextual classification rather than proving offence absence

sources.name: Online-crime flag consistency
verified_claims: online-crime flags are also often applied inconsistently within and across police forces
limitations: online flags must not be assumed complete

sources.name: Stalking classification and allocation
verified_claims: different stalking categories carry different maximum sentences
recording the wrong category can allocate the case to the wrong type of investigator
limitations: classification error is an operational-quality risk, not a parcel-risk value

sources.name: Regional registrar knowledge sharing
verified_claims: regional force-crime-registrar groups discuss counting-rule interpretations to support consistent application
limitations: regional agreement cannot eliminate all national variation
